question: Can host-side execution enforce Aion transition legality, affordability, registration, and STOP without granting model output authority over callbacks?
hypothesis: A deterministic executor that derives every outcome from an immutable host plan and callback registry rejects all stop-triggering requests without invoking a callback and produces traces that can be verified without re-execution.
falsifier: A forced, explicit, illegal, unaffordable, or unregistered request invokes a callback; an executed trace is accepted when its action, cost, budget, or plan binding differs from host inputs; or a replay requires invoking the original callback.
scope: Artificial engineering fixtures and no-side-effect API/web dry runs only; no LLM capability claim, protected evaluation, real tool operation, scientific training, model promotion, paid compute, or external communication.

history.event: Initial Torch-free executor and API, CLI and web fixtures implemented; nine focused tests passed while surface tests were resource-blocked.

Adversarial correction bound traces to immutable plans, full decisions and registered-action snapshots; rejected non-finite economics and inconsistent trace fields; removed all callback invocation from offline verification. Twelve focused tests, Ruff and strict MyPy passed. Surface integration remains resource-blocked.

Added an immutable multi-step execution ledger that binds the complete requested decision sequence, carries budget between traces, records ignored post-STOP requests, and rejects discontinuous or nonterminal STOP chains. Fifteen focused tests, Ruff and strict MyPy passed.
